issues: Nearly identical to its sister shot: the same violet-orange neon and the same small-type light workspace, so the two cards were indistinguishable
The 'orbit' was just a flat board rotating; the random background frames ignored perspective, so you could not feel the camera moving around
The lift was a 2D in-plane offset, so the rotation never revealed layers between components and panel
Panel type was 12–17px, even harder to read while rotating, and the final framing leaned to one side
changes: Switched to the midnight look: blue-to-cyan neon around a dark-glass analytics dashboard, Signal (124px headline number, area chart, three 58px KPIs, channel bars, goal ring), clearly separated from the sister shot's violet-pink light workspace

Built as a real 3D world: panel, floating parts, a reflective floor grid and eight vertical light pillars at different depths share one preserve-3d space, so the rotateY +36°→−24° orbit shows three layers of parallax

Parts float at 150–210px from the first frame so the layers read during the first half of the orbit; at 52f they all fall together and land on the same frame at 76f, where the whole tube flares once as the shot's single beat
A screen-space shift proportional to rotateY keeps the panel centered; the area chart draws while floating, its end point pulses after landing, and the pillars go out middle-first
Duration 140→150f: the orbit stops at 124f, leaving a 26f settle
